A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERM research framework. The complete main texts, figures, table, equations, and Appendices A–G are available and support reliable matching across the revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original teacher–student simulations, MNIST classification results, and regularizer-direction experiments, including empirical errors and score distributions.

after.justification: v4 retains original bimodal-regression simulations and MNIST classification results in Figures 1–3 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The ERM objective, deterministic objective J, and core fixed-point equations remain the same. The corrected introductory quadratic surrogate matches the surrogate already defined in v2 Section 3. The revisions concern theoretical characterization and justification without establishing a different learning procedure.

E1.justification: v4 removes the Figure 4 scenario combining Gaussian coordinates with a bimodal second coordinate. Bimodal teacher–student regression and MNIST classification using digits {3,6} versus {4,7} remain; no new dataset or evaluated task is introduced.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain the same Gaussian-data surrogates and Gaussian-score approximations as comparators. The removed geometric analyses compare regularizer settings and projections, rather than distinct competing methods. Table 1 remains a survey of prior theoretical work.

E3.justification: The regularizer-angle sweep in v2 Figure 4 and the projected/null-direction controls in Figure 5 are removed. Retained experiments preserve their reported settings, including p=30 and n=50 in Figure 1. Its newly explicit loss and regularizer specifications document the existing experiment without establishing a rerun or changed setting.

E4.justification: v4 removes the numerical analyses supporting regularizer geometry: Figure 4 tests how regularizer direction affects error and score Gaussianity, while Figure 5 examines objective variation and score distributions under subspace projections. This eliminates the empirical sensitivity and geometric-validation component; the new analytical example in Section 7 does not replace those experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Retained plots have unchanged uncertainty displays. Changes to theoretical concentration bounds are mathematical revisions, not changes in experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The plot content in Figures 1–3 is unchanged. v4 removes supporting results from Figures 4–5: angle-dependent errors and score distributions, directional objective curves, and projected-score distributions. Thus supporting findings disappear, while the principal regression and MNIST results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 replaces full-sample sub-Gaussian concentration with samplewise Poincare assumptions in the proportional regime, with corresponding moment-bound revisions. Assumption 4 enlarges permitted direction norms from O(1) to O(sqrt(n)), while Theorem 6.1 restricts observables to bounded Lipschitz functions. v4 adds explicit interchange/stability hypotheses, corrects the ridge mean and risk formulas in Corollary 5.1, and replaces unadjusted subspace confinement with a covariance-adjusted theorem for Gaussian residual noise. Appendices B–F contain substantial corresponding proof revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the claim about equivalence of any C2 regularizer. The contributions now specify smooth, strongly convex, weakly separable regularizers and equivalence of the first two score moments. The main characterization is explicitly conditional on the conjectural comparison principle and stability conditions, and the confinement contribution is redefined around covariance-adjusted geometry and Gaussian residual noise.

C2.justification: Section 7 now explains why anisotropic residual covariance can move the estimator mean outside the informative subspace. Section 6 corrects the assertion that conditional-mixture non-Gaussianity comes solely from its mean: varying conditional variance can also generate it. Figure 1's discussion resolves the earlier inconsistent description of squared-loss performance universality despite non-Gaussian scores.

D1.justification: Figure 1 newly specifies independent bimodal entries, the squared-norm regularizer, and the explicit elastic-loss formula. These improve documentation of the retained experiment. The code-access statement is unchanged, and no additional hardware, solver, runtime, or detailed MNIST processing information is supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds Louart's 2026 CLT preprint and removes Adamczak (2015), Louart's 2023 thesis, and Rockafellar–Wets (1998). The related-work taxonomy and Table 1 remain unchanged. Appendix F refines the existing connection to Mai–Liao's LFMM equations without introducing a new overarching research position.

P1.justification: The contributions, explanatory passages in Sections 2 and 4–7, and substantial portions of the appendix derivations are rewritten. Conditional headings and explanations become more explicit, the LFMM presentation is reorganized, and Appendix G loses repeated introductory definitions. This is extensive prose revision despite preservation of the main section sequence.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 are deleted rather than relocated, Table 1 moves from PDF page 4 to page 3, and Figure 1's caption is rewritten. The remaining plots and table retain their visual content and structure, and the overall main-text and appendix layout styles remain stable.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects important mathematical deficiencies: Corollary 5.1 accounts for nonzero feature means, observation noise, and loss normalization, while Theorem 7.1 replaces the incorrect unadjusted confinement claim with covariance-adjusted geometry and a new proof. Revised assumptions and conditional derivations also improve the calibration of the claims. These gains substantially improve this theory-focused paper despite losing Figures 4–5. The framework remains conjectural, and conditions discussed in prose are still not fully restated in Theorem 4.3.
